Attacker controls the full URL path; percent-encoding is decoded AFTER the only dot-normalization step, so %2e%2e (%2e%2e%2f) survives undot and becomes literal ../ in self.vpath.
F1_cpr_static_channel.sink: httpcli.py:783 self.tx_file(static_path) with static_path = os.path.join(self.E.mod, 'web/', self.vpath[5:]) (httpcli.py:782). tx_file then performs bos.stat(fs_path) (httpcli.py:2610), bos.open(fs_path, os.O_RDONLY) (httpcli.py:2615), open_func(*open_args) = open(fsenc(fs_path),'rb') (httpcli.py:2728-2735, 2772) and transfers content via os.sendfile (httpcli.py:2773-2775). This is a real file-read-and-respond operation, not a mere string concatenation.
F1_cpr_static_channel.allowed_root: self.E.mod/web/ - the copyparty application's bundled web-asset directory. Nothing in the vulnerable revision confines the joined result to it (no absreal/realpath, no startswith containment, no whitelist).

guard_analysis.vfs_get_undot_423: VFS.get(self.vpath,...) is called at httpcli.py:423 and does apply the load-bearing post-decode undot barrier (authsrv.py:473) to its own rem result - but the .cpr branch at :766-:783 re-reads the raw attribute self.vpath directly (vpath[5:]) and never uses the undot'd rem, so the barrier does not apply to this channel.

F2_doc_viewer.sink: httpcli.py:3875 docpath = os.path.join(abspath, doc); :3876 bos.path.getsize(docpath); :3878 open(fsenc(docpath),'rb') + f.read() sent to client.

F2_doc_viewer.guard_analysis: httpcli.py:3874 - membership whitelist: `if next((x for x in files if x['name'] == doc), None):` - doc must exactly equal the name of a file actually present in the current directory listing (files comes from vn.ls -> statdir/scandir at authsrv.py:515-554, so names are real single-component basenames; scandir never yields '..' or multi-segment names). The check executes before the join/open (:3874 < :3875/:3878) and is an exact string equality against on-disk entries, not a prefix check, not resolve(), not mere authentication. A doc containing ../ or an absolute path simply fails the membership test and falls into the '( textfile not found )' branch. Additionally requires can_read (:3869).

F4_xff_dip_suffix_family.source: httpcli.py:282 `zso = self.headers.get('x-forwarded-for')` - label P1-S-0109 (http_header family, tp). Genuinely header-derived, but only honored when self.args.rproxy is set AND the connection peer is 127.0.0.1/::1 (httpcli.py:283); the selected element zsl[n].strip() (:289/:291) is attacker-influenceable only in specific reverse-proxy configurations. It is not a path-shaped input - all 40 http_header tp labels were auto-extracted as generic self.headers.get(...) reads, so this source family is over-generalized for path-traversal purposes (checklist item 9).
F4_xff_dip_suffix_family.propagation: self.ip -> dip() (httpcli.py:515-519: self.ip.replace(':','.') only when args.plain_ip, otherwise iphash.s(self.ip) = one-way hash) -> suffix = '-{:.6f}-{}'.format(time.time(), dip) (httpcli.py:1455, :2186) -> params['suffix'] (:1461) / open_args (:2187) -> ren_open(fname, ..., suffix=...) (httpcli.py:1519/:1561/:2190/:2233) -> util.py ren_open: fpath = os.path.join(fdir, fname) (clean fname), and ONLY on filename collision `if suffix and os.path.lexists(fsenc(fpath)): fpath += suffix; fname += suffix` (util.py:1211-1214) -> open(fsenc(fpath)) (util.py:1216) and downstream joins/unlinks/stats/renames (httpcli.py:1521/:1531/:1564/:1584/:1607/:2254/:2255/:2281/:2337; util.py:1221, 1548, 1962-1965).
F4_xff_dip_suffix_family.filename_channel_is_sanitized: the actual upload filename always passes sanitize_fn(fn, '', bad) (httpcli.py:1473, :2176; util.py:1691: fn.replace('\\','/').split('/')[-1]) before any join - basename-only, so the fn channel itself cannot traverse; taint surviving past it is basename taint, which carries no path structure.
F4_xff_dip_suffix_family.why_not_exploitable: the only branch where the tainted suffix can enter a path string is the collision append `fpath += suffix` (util.py:1212). For that to traverse, the suffix must contain '/' and the path segment formed by '<existing-file>-<time.time() with 6 decimals>-<ip>' immediately before the first '/' would have to be an ALREADY-EXISTING DIRECTORY (kernel path resolution requires each pre-'..' segment to exist). That directory name embeds the current request's microsecond-precision server timestamp, which the attacker cannot predict or pre-create (they would have to MKCOL the exact directory name between the suffix computation and the open, microseconds apart).
F4_xff_dip_suffix_family.preconditions_stacked: (1) --rproxy > 0 with the connection arriving from loopback; (2) attacker control of the selected XFF element; (3) --plain_ip enabled (otherwise dip() hashes the value); (4) authenticated write access to a volume (PUT/POST upload); (5) filename collision (target file already exists) AND a pre-created directory whose name matches the unpredictable microsecond timestamp.
F4_xff_dip_suffix_family.barrier_evidence: sanitize_fn basename barrier (httpcli.py:1473/:2176) on the fn channel; _assert_safe_rem (httpcli.py:197-200) on the upload rem; VFS.get undot barrier (authsrv.py:473) on fdir (fdir = canonical(rem) from the guarded vpath, never from the XFF value).
F4_xff_dip_suffix_family.residual_note: a defense-in-depth concern exists in theory (raw header bytes reaching a filename suffix), but no realistic traversal write/read; classified likely_fp with the residual documented.

checklist_answers.1_source_attacker_controlled: Yes for F1 (full URL path, unauthenticated), F2 (query param) and F4 (XFF header element, conditional). F3's source is the URL path but it never reaches the read path in value terms.
checklist_answers.2_source_reaches_file_access: F1: yes, verifiably through vpath[5:]/join/tx_file with no intermediate normalization. F4: yes through dip/suffix/ren_open, but only into a collision-avoidance suffix. F2/F3: the reported edges terminate before an unguarded access (guard at :3874; dict confusion for 'ap').
checklist_answers.3_sink_is_sensitive_operation: F1: yes (stat, open, sendfile -> full file disclosure). F3/F4 sinks are real reads/writes/deletes but the values reaching them are neutralized. Pure concatenations were not counted as sinks (tx_file/ren_open/yieldfile are genuine access wrappers).
checklist_answers.4_declared_roots_and_escape: F1's root is E.mod/web/ and is escapable (that is the vulnerability). F2/F3/F4 roots are volume dirs guarded by undot (VFS.get), listing membership, or sanitize_fn basename.
checklist_answers.5_traversal_vectors: F1: %-encoded dot-segments survive the pre-decode undot (decode at :375 happens after), absolute-path injection via os.path.join absolute-component semantics, %-encoded separators. Windows-only relchk blocks backslash variants there. Symlinks: canonical/dcanonical TOCTOU shapes exist on other channels (per notes) but are not part of these alerts.
checklist_answers.6_real_guards: F2: exact listing-membership whitelist before access (effective). F3: undot barrier on rem (effective). F4: sanitize_fn basename (effective on the fn channel). F1: NO effective guard - that is the finding.
checklist_answers.7_misjudged_guards: The pre-decode undot at :333/:337 was correctly NOT treated as a barrier (unsound vs percent-encoding); no finding was dismissed merely because of Path.resolve/normpath/startswith or login checks. dip()'s hash is a value transform, not relied on as a barrier.
checklist_answers.8_authorized_normal_service: F2 (doc viewer) and F3 (zip download) are authorized features with effective guards. F4's upload machinery is authorized write behavior; the XFF suffix carries no practical traversal. F1 is NOT normal service: the .cpr static branch escapes its asset root.
checklist_answers.9_overgeneralization_causes: F3 is a dict-container value confusion (classic FP mechanism). F4 stems from the http_header label family auto-classifying every self.headers.get (incl. x-forwarded-for, P1-S-0109) as a path source; the flow itself is real but the security effect is neutralized. F1 was the pre-registered primary expected alert and is genuine.
checklist_answers.10_rule_purity: Only py/augur/copyparty/pass1-path-traversal is present (28 results, 4 codeFlows each); no diagnostics, no built-in CodeQL query results, no other CWEs mixed in.

summary: CodeQL analysis succeeded; the formal Pass 1 run produced 28 alerts under py/augur/copyparty/pass1-path-traversal. Independent re-review of all 28 codeFlows against the real source: 3 alerts are likely true positives - all anchored on the unauthenticated /.cpr static-asset traversal (GHSA-pxfv-7rr3-2qjg, fixed by commit 043e3c7), which is exactly the real vulnerability under review and IS hit by this pass. 25 alerts are likely false positives in two shapes: (a) effective pre-access guards the taint model cannot see (doc-viewer listing-membership whitelist; VFS.get undot on the zip channel), and (b) an X-Forwarded-For -> dip() -> collision-suffix chain in the upload temp-file machinery that is practically non-exploitable (basename sanitization plus a required unpredictably-timestamped directory).
